SYNTHETIC TEST FIXTURE - abridged paraphrase of the AI Act structure, NOT the legal text

THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND THE COUNCIL OF THE EUROPEAN UNION,

Whereas:

(1)

This fixture recital explains the purpose of harmonised rules for AI.

(2)

A second recital about trustworthy AI.

HAVE ADOPTED THIS REGULATION:

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 3

Definitions

For the purposes of this Regulation, the following definitions apply:

(1)

'AI system' means a machine-based system that infers from input how to generate outputs;

(4)

'deployer' means a person using an AI system under its authority;

Article 4

AI literacy

Providers and deployers shall take measures to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy of their staff.

CHAPTER II

PROHIBITED AI PRACTICES

Article 5

Prohibited AI practices

1. The following AI practices shall be prohibited:

(c)

social scoring leading to detrimental treatment;

(f)

AI systems to infer emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education institutions, except for medical or safety reasons;

2. Further conditions apply to biometric identification.

CHAPTER III

HIGH-RISK AI SYSTEMS

SECTION 3

Obligations of providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems

Article 27

Fundamental rights impact assessment for high-risk AI systems

1. Prior to deploying a high-risk AI system referred to in points 5 (b) and (c) of Annex III, deployers shall perform an assessment of the impact on fundamental rights.

2. The obligation applies to the first use of the system. Article 99

Penalties

3. Non-compliance with the prohibition of the AI practices referred to in Article 5 shall be subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 35 000 000 or up to 7 % of total worldwide annual turnover.

This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.

Done at Brussels, 1 January 2099.

For the European Parliament

The President

A. N. OTHER

ANNEX III

High-risk AI systems referred to in Article 6(2)

5. Access to essential private services:

(b) AI systems intended to be used to evaluate the creditworthiness of natural persons;

(c) AI systems intended to be used for risk assessment and pricing in relation to natural persons in the case of life and health insurance.
